title: consolidate-credential-prefetch-and-stream-api-hygiene
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs had duplicated fragile logic around credential prefetch/lease warmup and slightly divergent streaming ergonomics which caused intermittent auth races and inconsistent telemetry labels across Python/TS/Go. This PR centralizes prefetch/backoff presets, tightens stream lifecycle semantics, and harmonizes telemetry tags so multi-language integrations show coherent traces and cost attribution. Scope: 1) introduce a small cross-SDK contract (neutral JSON blob) that describes a credential prefetch profile (ttl_target_ms, warmup_window_ms, jitter_pct) and wire it into each SDK's credential manager; 2) surface a lightweight StreamHandle.close(reason) API in Python and TS and align Go CloseWithReason to match semantics (idempotent, synchronous drain then close); 3) add adaptive retry presets for auth failures (fast-fail under 401->refresh->retry) while preserving existing backoff defaults for network errors; 4) unify telemetry labels emitted by SDKs (session_id, cred_profile, retry_phase) and add an opt-in debug flag that enables per-request credential lifecycle spans; 5) bump SDK package minor versions (py 1.12.0, ts 2.4.1, go 1.5.0) and update changelogs. Risk and mitigation: exposing a common prefetch contract required verifying no consumer relied on previous implicit timing; we guarded rollout with environment-controlled feature-flag (REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH_V2) and added comprehensive integration tests. Backward compatibility: if the feature flag is off, SDKs behave exactly as before. Tests: added unit tests for credential window math, E2E smoke for stream close semantics in CI. Rollout: staged release — first neural infra and internal apps enabled the flag for two days, monitoring showed no auth regressions, then general availability. See release notes. Related work: follows ENG-9023 (credential resilience) and ENG-9102 (stream ergonomics parity).
commits_summary: 3 commits: a) introduce cred_profile schema + serializer and tests; b) SDK bindings: py/ts/go credential manager wiring and stream handle close semantics; c) docs + changelogs + version bumps and CI matrix tweak to run session-telemetry tests.
changed_snippets:
// credential_profile.py: validate and normalize profile
def normalize(profile): return {"ttl_target_ms": int(profile.get('ttl_target_ms', 30000)), "warmup_window_ms": int(profile.get('warmup_window_ms', 5000)), "jitter_pct": float(profile.get('jitter_pct', 0.12)) }

// stream/handle.ts: idempotent close with reason
async close(reason?: string){ if(this._closed) return; await this._drain(); this._closed = true; this._emitClose(reason);}

// profile.go: small helper to compute prefetch deadline
func PrefetchDeadline(now time.Time, ttlMs int, warmupMs int) time.Time { return now.Add(time.Duration(ttlMs-warmupMs) * time.Millisecond) }
review_thread_summary: Reviewer Ethan: requested clearer invariants for idempotent close and asked for a synchronous close test; Claire: requested telemetry label naming follow tracing conventions and asked to gate the new debug spans behind an env var; Ravi: asked for explicit retry-presets mapping and suggested a short integration test for auth-401 refresh path. Author responses: implemented synchronous close test and added EnsureClosed idempotency guard; renamed telemetry labels to session_id/cred_profile/retry_phase; added REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH_V2 env gate and REVIEWERS noted CI flakiness fixed by small sleep in test harness. Approvals: Ethan approved after patch, Claire approved after label rename, Ravi approved after adding the 401->refresh integration test. CI: initial run had one flaky test (stream_close race) failing; fixed by adding deterministic drain hook and rerun succeeded.
release_notes: Unified credential prefetch contract and stream close ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Introduces REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH_V2 feature flag, new telemetry labels (session_id, cred_profile, retry_phase), and minor version bumps: py 1.12.0, ts 2.4.1, go 1.5.0. Backwards compatible when feature flag is disabled.
notes_for_cherrypick: Backport to release/1.11.x only required for python SDK where internal users depend on earlier behavior; use feature-flag guarded cherrypick to avoid behavioural change by default.
